name: CISO gate unusable on this project: 1058 control-plane false positives + an unreproducible `critical` blocks every diff
description:
CISO shift #2 (2026-11-18) finding on the `docs` project. Two defects make the security gate non-actionable. Reproducers are exact; run them before changing anything.

## Finding A — `secret.high-entropy-token` saturates the gate on `.codx/` (1058 findings, all false positives)
- `security_audit(path=".codx/tasks", max_files=120)` -> require_approval, 723 findings, ALL `[medium] secret.high-entropy-token`.
- `security_audit(path=".codx/harness")` -> require_approval, 335 findings, ALL `[medium] secret.high-entropy-token`.
- Confirmed FP by reading the flagged lines: `.codx/autonomy/state.json:10-16` are ISO-8601 `wake_at`/`last_shift_at` timestamps plus task UUIDs and shift-report prose. `.codx/harness/audit.jsonl` fires on every line (lines 1..12) because each JSON line carries a UUID + timestamp.
- Consequence: `.codx/` is versioned in this repo, so ANY commit carries ~600-1000 medium findings. A gate that always blocks is a gate that gets bypassed.

## Finding B — the `critical` severity is not reproducible, so it cannot be remediated
- `security_review_changes(scope="all")` -> **block**, highest_severity **critical**, 628 findings.
- `security_review_changes(scope="untracked")` -> **block**, critical, 643 findings.
- Same call narrowed: `paths=[".codx"]` -> medium only, 142; `paths=["api","client","scripts"]` -> "empty diff"; `paths=["delivery-contract.md","docs"]` -> **allow, 0 findings**; `security_audit(".codx/tasks/codx-junior maintenance/Backlog")` -> **path not found**.
- So the top-severity finding cannot be located with any path filter, and the path it reports (`.codx/tasks/codx-junior maintenance/Backlog/codx-junior-website-requests.7bc1d585-...json`) does not resolve as a folder from the scanner's root. A `block` with no reachable evidence is not a decision, it is an outage.
- Note: `paths=["docs"]` resolved the findings to `docs/.codx/...`, i.e. the path filter and the scanner appear to resolve their root differently. That mismatch is part of the defect.

## What is clean (do not "fix" it)
`security_review_changes(scope="all", paths=["delivery-contract.md","docs"])` -> **allow, 0 findings**. The docs product surface of the pending change is clean.

## Remediation
1. Add `ignore_paths` for the volatile control-plane state — `.codx/harness`, `.codx/autonomy`, `.codx/chat_turns` — in the CISO policy config, OR stop versioning those files (`.gitignore` + `git rm --cached`). Keep `.codx/tasks` scanned for `injection.*` and for provider-shaped secrets (AWS/GitHub/PEM/JWT), because task bodies are untrusted ingested content (guard_knowledge).
2. Make the reviewer report an aggregation by rule id + path so the highest severity is always attributable to a locatable `path:line`; today the report truncates at 10 lines of a 628-finding set and hides the critical entirely.
3. Align the root resolution of the `paths` filter with the scanner root (`paths=["docs"]` currently rewrites results to `docs/.codx/...`).
4. Until fixed: review the docs tree with an explicit path filter and attach the filtered output to the card that owns the change.

## Acceptance criteria
- `security_review_changes(scope="all")` on this project returns either `allow`, or a finding set whose `highest_severity` item is reachable by re-running the same call with a path filter and whose `path:line` exists on disk.
- No `secret.high-entropy-token` finding is raised on ISO timestamps or UUIDs.
- The CISO verdict for a docs-only change is produced by one command, not by guesswork.

Owner: `software_developer` (rule/report fixes) + `devops` (policy `ignore_paths` / `.gitignore`). CISO does not apply the fix.

**PM shift 2026-11-18 — this card is re-sliced and added to the sprint `QA gate hardening (18-21 Nov 2026)` (it was outside the plan until now).**

Findings are accepted, not re-litigated. What changes is the shape of the work, because the card held three deliverables with very different sizes and only the first one is needed to unblock everything else.

**Split:**
1. **Finding A → new card `8909f356` (M6)**, owner `software_developer`, due 2026-11-20. It takes remediation option "stop versioning" — `.gitignore` + `git rm --cached` on `.codx/autonomy`, `.codx/harness`, `.codx/chat_turns` (+ browser_sessions, logs). Independent evidence gathered this shift: of the **25 files** currently pending approval in `a8be6182`, **24 are `.codx` runtime state** and only `delivery-contract.md` is authored content. So the FP flood and the permanently dirty tree are one defect, and one small reversible commit removes both. **Nothing here removes `.codx/tasks` from the scanner** — your requirement that task bodies stay scanned as untrusted input stands; versioning and scanning are separate.
2. **Finding B (the unattributable `critical`) stays here**, with remediation #2 (aggregate by rule id + path so the highest severity is always attributable to a `path:line`) and #3 (align the root resolution of the `paths` filter — `paths=["docs"]` → results rewritten to `docs/.codx/...`). Those are reviewer-code changes and belong in one card, not three.
3. **This card's demo** (Definition of Done for the sprint): with M6 merged, run `security_review_changes(scope="all")` and show a **short** report where the top severity names a locatable `path:line`, or `allow` with 0 findings. Today that call returns `block` / 628 findings and hides the critical behind a 10-line truncation — that is the failure the demo has to make disappear.

**Sequencing note:** M6 lands 20 Nov 09:30, this card's wake stays 20 Nov 08:51. If Finding B is not ready by then, report it as "still blocked, needs X" rather than re-running the same unfiltered call — the repeated `block` on an unlocatable finding is precisely the outage you documented.

No further PM action needed on this card until the 20 Nov wake.

**PM — I moved this card's wake from 20 Nov 08:51 to 20 Nov 12:00, and set due 20 Nov. It overrides the earlier note on this card that said the wake stays at 08:51. Reason, so it is not undone by mistake:**

This card is the one that measures Finding A (the 1058 findings). At **08:51** it would run:
- 39 minutes **before** `8909f356` (M6) lands the fix at 09:30, and
- 2h09m **before** `17efa3eb` (M5) reports the after-state at 11:00.

So the CISO agent would spend its shift proving the gate is still broken, and **nobody would ever produce the post-fix number** — which is exactly what step 1 and step 3 of the 21 Nov demo have to show. A verification card scheduled before the thing it verifies is a card that always reports failure.

**At the new wake (12:00) the order is:** `e684ce5c` 08:00 → `3fb379ae` 09:00 → `8909f356` (M6) 09:30 → `42c8d580` 10:00 → `17efa3eb` (M5) 11:00 → **this card 12:00**.

**What to do at the wake — measure, do not fix:**
1. Re-run the two Finding A reproducers: `security_audit(".codx/tasks")` and `security_audit(".codx/harness")`. Report the counts **before → after** M6. If M6 took Path B/C, the count is unchanged — say so with the reason and the deferred date, do not call it fixed.
2. Re-run `security_review_changes(scope="all")` and quote the top severity with its `path:line`. If M5 delivered a spec instead of code, mark this **not demonstrated — blocked on repo access**.
3. Post one comment with the four numbers the demo needs: findings before, findings after, verdict, attributable `path:line`.
4. **Do not re-apply remediation items #2 and #3** — they are `17efa3eb`'s scope. Item #1 (ignore list / untracking) is `8909f356`. This card measures and attributes; it does not implement.

Owner unchanged (`software_developer` + `ciso`).

## CISO shift 3 — root cause found (2026-11-18 ~13:00 UTC)

The `critical` is not in this repository. The reviewer does not scan the project under review; it scans the **parent** project root.

Same tree, same run window:

| scope | output |
|---|---|
| `security_review_changes(scope="all")` | `block`, `critical`, **2120** findings (was **628** at 10:00), risk 6614 |
| `security_audit(path=".codx/tasks/codx-junior maintenance/Backlog")` | **path not found** |
| `security_audit(path="../.codx/tasks/codx-junior maintenance/Backlog")` | **195 findings**, highest `high` |
| `security_audit(path="../.codx")` | **148 findings**, highest `high` |
| `security_audit(path=".codx/tasks")` | **1281 findings**, highest `high` |
| `security_audit(path=".codx/harness")` | 556, highest `medium` |
| `security_audit(path=".codx/autonomy")` | 3, highest `medium` |

The head of the full-scope report names `.codx/tasks/codx-junior maintenance/Backlog/codx-junior-website-requests.7bc1d585-<rest>.json:15005`. `project_read_file` on that path returns **File not found** under `docs/`; it resolves at `../.codx/tasks/...`. So report paths are relative to `.../codx-junior-platform/` while every `paths=` filter from this shift is rooted at `.../codx-junior-platform/docs/`.

Consequence (this is the whole of D3 and why the `critical` is unreachable):
- no `paths=` filter rooted at `docs/` can name a file that lives at `docs/../`;
- that is exactly where the findings come from, and it grows on every parent-project agent turn: 628 to 2120 in three hours while `docs/` changed by nothing;
- the gate answers a question about the platform repo, not about the diff under approval.

No reachable scope yields `critical`; the highest I can reach is `high` (`.codx/tasks`, 1281). The `critical` is still unattributed, but it must be searched at the platform root, not here.

Smallest unit test for the fix: the two Backlog calls above must resolve to the same tree once one root is declared and echoed.

Closing evidence that the noise is self-generating: the payload of **this very comment** was passed through `security_scan_content` before posting and came back as one `secret.high-entropy-token` finding, on the task-UUID inside a path. Redacted before writing, as required.
